failure_reason: Akamai bot-manager interstitial ('Powered and protected by...') became a persistent, site-wide block partway through the run. robots.txt had no Claude-specific disallow, and the Chrome connector initially worked well (homepage, furniture.html department hub, and 7 sub-department hub pages all loaded fully, plus 3 leaf category listing pages rendered their true product counts). After the 3rd leaf-count read (sofas-couches.html), every subsequent costco.com navigation in the tab -- including a brand-new tab and re-requesting the very first URL that had worked cleanly (furniture.html) -- returned only the static Akamai interstitial shell and never resolved, even after foregrounding the tab (screenshot) and multiple retries/waits. This matches the brief's HARD BLOCK RULE (a real block, not a background-tab visibility artifact, since foregrounding did not clear it and it recurred across fresh tabs). Per that rule, browser requests to costco.com were stopped. 34 of 37 leaf categories could not have their exact qty verified and are recorded as null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag; the category tree itself (all group and leaf node names + canonical URLs) was fully and independently confirmed from the site's own 'Shop by Category' navigation on each department hub page before the block landed, so it is trustworthy even though most counts are not.
notes: ACCESS: robots.txt (https://www.costco.com/robots.txt) checked first -- no ClaudeBot/Claude-User/Claude-SearchBot/Claude-Web disallow anywhere; only generic legacy WCS view-pattern disallows, not a block signal. Reached entirely via the Claude-in-Chrome connector (own tab, no curl/WebFetch). STRUCTURE SOURCE: walked the Furniture department hub (costco.com/furniture.html) and then each of its 7 room/department sub-pages (living-room.html, bedroom-furniture.html, dining-kitchen.html, office-furniture.html, youth-furniture.html, entryway-furniture.html, patio-furniture.html) plus massage-chairs-cushions.html, reading each page's own 'Shop by Category' tile strip via same-tab JS (document.querySelectorAll('a[href]')) for the canonical child URLs -- this is the deepest-node tree, corroborated against the department hub's own nav links. Also checked game-room.html (game/pool tables -- game equipment, not furniture, excluded), storage-organization.html and storage-organization-kitchen.html (standalone storage/organizer departments, excluded per project rule -- only overlap was Kitchen Islands & Carts, already captured under Kitchen & Dining), and dining-collections.html (a named-collection sub-page under Kitchen & Dining Room Sets -- excluded per the collections/brand-listing rule, not a true category). QTY METHOD: rendered listing header 'Showing 1-24 of N', cross-checked against the left filter panel's own 'Delivery N results (N)' facet count on the same page -- both agreed exactly on all 3 verified leaves (69/37/38). EXCLUDED (checked, not furniture): Mattresses, indoor Fireplaces and Stoves, outdoor Fire Pit Sets (heating/fire feature not seating furniture), Chair Mats, Outdoor Umbrellas & Sun Shade Sails, Deck Boxes & Outdoor Storage Boxes, Outdoor Furniture Covers, Area Rugs, Home & Decorative Accents, Bookcases dup-URL handled once (placed under Office), Round/Square/Rectangular table-shape links and 5/7/8/9/10-Piece dining links (all self-referential JS filter buttons, not distinct category pages), Queen/King-size-filtered bedroom-set pages (not in the site's own 'Shop by Category' nav, a size filter variant of Bedroom Sets). Entryway Furniture department has only one furniture child (Console & Entryway Tables) which is already captured under Living Room via the same canonical URL, so no separate Entryway grouping row is emitted. Massage Chairs (massage-chairs-cushions.html) is a genuine seating-furniture leaf with no children, included standalone. 'Bookcases & Bookshelves' (office-furniture-bookcases.html) appears identically in both the Living Room and Office nav trees; emitted once, under Office, to avoid a duplicate row. 'Folding Tables & Chairs' (tables.html) similarly appears in both Kitchen & Dining and Office nav trees; emitted once, under Kitchen & Dining.
